newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher ahead of LME stock report.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher ahead of LME stock report.

text.p: COMEX copper settled at the day's high after making slow but steady gains as the market appeared to become convinced there will be a large draw down in LME stocks on Tuesday.

Although LME stocks have fallen sharply recently, prices have not responded as much as some traders hoped. Stocks fell nearly 20,000 tonnes Friday, and traders expected a draw of 10,000 to 20,000 tonnes Tuesday.
"With the amount we have seen drawndown in the past few weeks, it may have more of an impact tomorrow, and the market looks favorable to an upside test," a trader said.
December COMEX settled settled at 93.00 cents per pound, almost at a seven week high, and up 1.45 cents from Friday. December was traded 93.00 to 91.20 cents.
The close was technically bullish, above the five, ten, and twenty-day moving averages.
Meanwhile labor talks continue at Kennecott Utah Copper Corp which was hit by a brief strike at the end of last week.
Labor talks at Phelps Dodge Corp's Chino mine are also due to resume on October 24.
Employees at both companies are working without a labor contract.

Merrill Lynch said in a report that a large U.S. investment bank which took over Sumitomo copper positions, was trying to push prices higher but was meeting resistance from producers that are taking advantage of firmer prices to sell forward.

John Gross wrote in the Copper Journal newsletter that the copper market was still operating in a deficit and some 100,000 tons of red metal have been pulled out of COMEX and LME warehouses since early September - but the market has not rallied significantly.

"The backwardation is still with us and getting wider, indicating a firmer rather than easier fundamental balance," Gross said. "And the longer the market ignores these developments, the stronger the reaction will be when they are finally recognized."
